summary: All five Module 04 labs were re-run with tools/labrun.py (no --update) on the preparation machine (4 CPU threads): Lab 1 53 s, Lab 2 106 s, Lab 3 99 s, Lab 4 227 s, Lab 5 126 s. Every output block matched the fences written in 5cdb625 exactly, except Lab 5's wall-clock timing table, which varies run to run. To support some statements, extra runs were made from copies of the lab scripts in the scratchpad (lab code in the source unchanged, no new code blocks): Lab 2 with torch.manual_seed(7) in train_log_model (LSTM b_f=0 73.1%, b_f=1 96.4%, RNN 24.1% at update 2,500; about 33-35 s per model); Lab 3 with torch seed 1 (Step 2 RMSE 0.656 against naive 0.361, mean error -0.589; per-fold gain over linear AR 18/11/13/8%; excitation delay 85) and with QUICK = True (35 s; Step 2 0.648 against 0.361; excitation delay 125); Lab 3's alarm positions for the default run (offset point alarms at +0, +4, +100; stuck point alarm at +100, the recovery sample); Lab 4 beam diagnostics on the same run (beam log-probability >= greedy on 200/200 strings, digit accuracy over the 12 digits 49.9% beam against 48.6% greedy, beam ending early on 122 strings against greedy's 114); Lab 5 run_recall for seeds 0-4 (seed 0 reproduced the table exactly) and three further timing runs. The prose in the labs, in concept parts s4/s5/s8/s9/s10/s11/s13 and 'What goes wrong', in exercises e8 and e9 and in the practice summary was reconciled with the real outputs, including the qualitative changes: Lab 4's beam search now lowers token accuracy, Lab 5's vanilla RNN reaches 100% at lag 100 on two seeds of five, the FFT form is no faster at T = 4,096, Lab 3's recursive LSTM is worse than naive at h = 20, and the stuck sensor now raises one point alarm at its recovery. No figures (SVG or captions) and no plan display fields quote lab numbers, so none changed. node tools/check.mjs --module 4 --lang en --words reports 0 errors, 0 warnings.
